Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- The failing test XMLSpaceTest.testPreserveDOM expects leading/trailing whitespace to be preserved for a DOM-backed document when xml:space="preserve". It calls doTest("preserve", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, " foo "), which asserts that context.getValue("test/text[@id='preserve']") equals " foo ".
- The context is created from a DocumentContainer using the DOM model, so XPath resolution returns a DOM node pointer.
- In the DOM model, DOMNodePointer.getValue() delegates to stringValue(node).
- DOMNodePointer.stringValue(Node) unconditionally trims whitespace:
  - For text nodes and CDATA nodes: it returns node.getNodeValue().trim().
  - For comments and processing instructions: it trims as well.
  - For element nodes: it concatenates text from children and then returns buf.toString().trim().
- Because of these unconditional trim() calls, a text node whose content is " foo " is returned as "foo", which directly matches the reported issue “JXPath automatically trims string values” and causes the test to fail (expected " foo ", got "foo").
- The implementation does not consult the xml:space attribute (e.g., xml:space="preserve") on the node or its ancestors, so it cannot honor preservation semantics. It trims regardless of XML whitespace handling rules.

Root cause:
- Unconditional trimming in DOMNodePointer.stringValue for text, CDATA, and aggregated element content ignores xml:space="preserve", leading to removal of leading/trailing spaces and failing the preserve behavior expected by the test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
